scouting_result.scout_verdict:
At 196cm and 103kg, you occupy the court with a gravitational pull that few can contest. Your journey has been defined by a need for high-intensity, collaborative synergy, and in the standing discipline of basketball, your stature is the perfect anchor for a perimeter-to-paint offense. Every movement you make, from the snap of a screen to the explosive verticality in the lane, is a testament to the structured power development you have mastered. When you step onto the floor at The Games, your physical profile acts as the fulcrum for your entire unit, turning individual strength into collective dominance.

Your adaptive pathway, specifically through competitive wheelchair basketball, offers a profound evolution of this identity. This sport utilizes a functional classification system that groups athletes by their level of physical ability to ensure equitable, intense competition—often requiring players to master specialized maneuvering to compensate for lower-limb impairment while maintaining the same aggressive, high-speed pace you thrive in. Here, the tactical requirements shift toward a heightened sense of court geometry and rapid-fire ball handling, allowing you to project your collaborative intensity into a discipline where spatial awareness is the ultimate weapon.

scouting_result.scout_verdict:
Transitioning your focus from court-based agility to the singular, unyielding force of bobsleigh and push sports requires a shift toward pure, explosive kinetic transfer. At 103kg, you possess the raw mass and power capacity to generate the immense momentum required during the initial phase of the run—the 'push'—where every micro-second of explosive output dictates the potential for the entire descent. This is where your commitment to structured strength training becomes the defining factor, turning your body into an engine designed for one, singular, high-force release.

For your adaptive pathway, you find a distinct outlet in the F56 seated throws category. F56 denotes athletes with lower-limb impairment who compete from a fixed, seated position, requiring them to generate maximum power exclusively through the core, shoulders, and upper body. While your standing pathway leverages your full kinetic chain for speed, the seated throws demand a focused, technical precision that isolates your upper-body power. It is an environment of intense, meditative concentration—a complete contrast to the chaotic speed of the track, yet equally dependent on the explosive power development you have made the centerpiece of your journey toward The Games.
